name: Volt Typhoon
affiliation_detail:
Attributed by 2023 CISA advisory as a PRC state-sponsored group. No specific PLA unit, MSS bureau, or contractor firm has been publicly identified. 
New Jersey Cybersecurity & Communications Integration Cell (NJCCIC) assessed the group is "likely affiliated with the PLA or MSS." 
No indictments have been unsealed.
description:
According to the publicly available information, Volt Typhoon is assessed to be  a PRC state-sponsored group focused on pre-positioning within U.S. critical infrastructure for potential disruption or destruction during a future geopolitical crisis. (CISA, 2024)
Active since at least mid-2021, the group has compromised organizations in communications, energy, water, transportation, manufacturing, maritime, construction, government, IT, and education, with focus on strategic locations, including Guam. (Microsoft, 2023)
Volt Typhoon's behavior is not consistent with traditional espionage. CISA (2024) assessed the group is seeking to pre-position on IT networks for lateral movement to OT assets, collecting ICS/SCADA documentation including network diagrams and operations manuals.
According to Microsoft TI (2023), the group relies on living-off-the-land techniques — using native Windows tools, hands-on-keyboard activity, and stolen valid credentials rather than deploying custom malware. Traffic is routed through the KV Botnet, a network of compromised end-of-life SOHO routers (primarily Cisco and NETGEAR) that makes attack traffic appear to originate from legitimate U.S. IP addresses. Initial access typically exploits vulnerabilities in internet-facing Fortinet, Ivanti, NETGEAR, Citrix, and Cisco devices.
In January 2024, the FBI disrupted the KV Botnet via court-authorized operation, removing malware from hundreds of SOHO routers.

campaigns.name: U.S. Critical Infrastructure Pre-Positioning
campaigns.description: Sustained campaign targeting critical infrastructure in Guam and across the continental U.S. Compromised telecom companies, satellite operators, utilities, water systems, and transportation hubs. Initial access via Fortinet FortiGuard and other internet-facing appliance vulnerabilities. CISA confirmed five-year persistence in some environments and collection of ICS/SCADA documentation. Microsoft and the U.S. government assessed the activity as pre-positioning for potential disruption during a future crisis, particularly regarding Taiwan scenarios.

campaigns.name: KV Botnet Operations
campaigns.description: Construction and operation of the KV Botnet — a covert relay network of compromised SOHO routers used to proxy attack traffic and conceal origins. Black Lotus Labs documented the botnet in December 2023. FBI disrupted it via court order in January 2024, removing malware from hundreds of routers. Volt Typhoon rapidly rebuilt the infrastructure. SecurityScorecard reported 30% of Cisco RV320/325 devices compromised in 37 days.
